title: Unit normalization and scalar transposition of a commuting realization cube
statement: For arbitrary categories and adjunctions the following three algebraic identities hold. (1) Let E_A:A≌C and E_B:B≌D, a:S⊣U with S:C→D, and b:T⊣V with T:A→B. Given k:U E_A^{-1}≅E_B^{-1} V, define c:E_B U≅V E_A by inserting the counit of E_A, applying E_B k E_A, and cancelling E_B E_B^{-1} by its unit. If r:E_A S≅T E_B is the unit-preserving left-adjoint uniqueness comparison determined by k, then η_a(E_A X);U(r_X);c_{TX}=E_A(η_b(X)). (2) Let F_ZA,F_ZB,F_YA,F_YB and I_ZA,I_ZB,I_YA,I_YB be eight categories, with realization functors E_ZA,E_ZB,E_YA,E_YB from the F categories to the corresponding I categories. Let S_Z⊣U_Z and S_Y⊣U_Y be scalar adjunctions on I and T_Z⊣V_Z and T_Y⊣V_Y scalar adjunctions on F. Let P_A,P_B:I_Z→I_Y and Q_A,Q_B:F_Z→F_Y. Suppose r_Z:E_ZA S_Z≅T_Z E_ZB, r_Y:E_YA S_Y≅T_Y E_YB, c_Z:E_ZB U_Z≅V_Z E_ZA and c_Y:E_YB U_Y≅V_Y E_YA satisfy the unit equations in (1), and d_A:E_ZA P_A≅Q_A E_YA, d_B:E_ZB P_B≅Q_B E_YB, h:U_Z P_A≅P_B U_Y, t:V_Z Q_A≅Q_B V_Y satisfy P_A(c_Z(L));d_A(V_Z L);E_YA(t_L)=h(E_ZB L);U_Y(d_B(L));c_Y(Q_B L). Write α_K for the scalar transpose of P_A(η_Z(E_ZA K));h(S_Z E_ZA K), and β_K for the scalar transpose of Q_A(η_Z(K));t(T_Z K). Then α_K;P_B(r_Z(K));d_B(T_Z K)=S_Y(d_A(K));r_Y(Q_A K);E_YB(β_K). (3) Given geometric adjunctions L_A⊣Q_A,L_B⊣Q_B and scalar adjunctions T_Y⊣V_Y,T_Z⊣V_Z, suppose isomorphisms s:V_Y L_A≅L_B V_Z, e:L_A T_Z≅T_Y L_B and t:V_Z Q_A≅Q_B V_Y satisfy mate(T_Y⊣V_Y,T_Z⊣V_Z,e.hom)=s.hom and mate(L_B⊣Q_B,L_A⊣Q_A,s.hom)=t.inv. Then the scalar transpose of Q_A(η_Z(K));t(T_Z K) equals mate(L_A⊣Q_A,L_B⊣Q_B,e.inv)_K. Composition is written left to right. These identities impose no preservation, nonemptiness or exactness hypotheses.

proof.text: Use the unit equation for leftAdjointUniq to identify its conjugate with k.inv. The iterated-mates identity and the explicit inverse mate formula identify its scalar mate with c.inv. The unit_mateEquiv equation, followed by c.hom, proves (1).

For (2), apply the injective scalar Hom-equivalence at Y and postcompose with c_Y. Replace the transpose followed by its unit by its defining map, move r_Z through h by naturality, apply the cube equation, and use (1) at Z. Naturality of d_A moves the fixed scalar unit to Y; naturality of c_Y and (1) at Y identify the other path. The remaining equality is the defining Hom-equivalence equation for β. All these operations are written and proved in Lean.

For (3), the iterated-mates formula identifies the conjugate of e.hom with t.inv. conjugateIsoEquiv sends inverses to inverses, so the iterated mate of e.inv is t.hom. Apply unit_mateEquiv and the scalar Hom-equivalence to obtain the displayed transpose.

theorem realizationScalar_unit (X : A) :
    a.unit.app (EA.functor.obj X) ≫
        U.map ((((EA.toAdjunction.comp a).ofNatIsoRight k).leftAdjointUniq
          (b.comp EB.toAdjunction)).hom.app X) ≫
        (realizationRestrictionFromInverse EA EB k).hom.app (T.obj X) =
      EA.functor.map (b.unit.app X)
